library(knowledge)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

```{r load}
# data from data-raw/vignette_chinook.R
vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "knowledge", mustWork = TRUE)
x <- readRDS(vd("chinook_rearing.rds"))
seg <- readRDS(vd("bulk_segments.rds"))
water <- readRDS(vd("bulk_water.rds"))

tune <- x$tune
summ <- x$summary
meta <- x$meta
cmp <- x$compare
dflt <- tune[tune$is_default, ]
rec <- tune[tune$recommended %in% TRUE, ]
region <- tune[tune$in_region, ]
all_row <- cmp[cmp$watershed_group_code == "ALL", ]
per_group <- cmp[cmp$watershed_group_code != "ALL", ]
map_row <- cmp[cmp$watershed_group_code == meta$map_group, ]
seeds <- x$seeds
honest <- x$honest

# formatting
n0 <- function(v) format(round(v), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
n1 <- function(v) format(round(v, 1), big.mark = ",", nsmall = 1, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
pc <- function(v, d = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * v, format = "f", digits = d), " %")
grad <- function(g) paste0(signif(100 * g, 3), " %")
km_d <- function(d) if (d >= 1000) paste(format(d / 1000, trim = TRUE), "km") else paste(d, "m")
lst <- function(v, and = "and") if (length(v) < 2) v else paste(paste(v[-length(v)], collapse = ", "), and, v[length(v)])
words <- function(r) {
  size <- if (r$size_var == "mad") sprintf("a mean annual flow of at least %s m³/s", format(r$size_min, trim = TRUE))
          else sprintf("a channel at least %s m wide", format(r$size_min, trim = TRUE))
  exc <- if (is.na(r$exc_q)) ""
         else sprintf(", or a river of at least %s m³/s within %s downstream", r$exc_q, km_d(r$exc_d))
  sprintf("a gradient of at most %s, and %s%s", grad(r$grad_max), size, exc)
}
share_of <- function(col, v) sum(tune$boot_rec_share[tune[[col]] %in% v])
no_grad <- function(rule) sub("\\|g<=[0-9.]+\\|", "|", rule)
seed_other <- tune[tune$rule %in% seeds$recommended[no_grad(seeds$recommended) != no_grad(rec$rule)], ]
seed_same_shape <- sum(no_grad(seeds$recommended) == no_grad(rec$rule))

# the saved curves give exp(fit - fit at the threshold) on the cloglog scale, a ratio of hazards; the
# rates are the fitted chances themselves
grad_at <- function(g) {
  d <- x$curves[x$curves$curve == "gradient", ]
  stats::approx(d$x, d$rate, xout = g)$y
}

link_site <- "https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/link/"
fresh_site <- "https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/fresh/"
link_default <- sprintf("https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/link/tree/%s/inst/extdata/configs/default", meta$link_sha)
```

New Graph Environment maps where fish can live in British Columbia's streams with
[`link`](`r link_site`), an R package that marks every segment of the provincial stream
network as spawning or rearing habitat for each species, and as reachable by fish or not. It does
this with a **configuration**: a set of rules and thresholds for stream size and steepness, one
set per species and life stage. Its standard configuration is called
[`default`](`r link_default`). Its thresholds start from the ones
[`bcfishpass`](https://github.com/smnorris/bcfishpass) has used for years, a project New Graph
contributes to.

This article tests one of those rules, where juvenile chinook salmon rear, against the province's
electrofishing records: places crews fished, and whether they caught chinook. It asks which
version of the rule the records support, how sure that answer is, and what the chosen rule
changes on the ground. The tests are part of `knowledge`, the R package this article belongs to.

**The answer.** The records support a different rule from `default`: **`r words(rec)`**.
`default` asks for `r words(dflt)`. The new rule draws less habitat, `r n1(-all_row$change_pct)` %
fewer km across the province, and separates where chinook are caught from where they are not
more sharply.

## What does link draw for chinook rearing now?

Under `default`, a segment is chinook rearing habitat when chinook can reach it and one of
four tests holds:

- **stream**: a single-line stream or canal, not one drawn through a wetland, with a gradient of
  at most `r grad(dflt$grad_max)` and a channel at least `r dflt$size_min` m wide;
- **river**: inside a river polygon, at the same gradient, any width;
- **wetland**: inside a wetland of at least 1 ha;
- **lake**: inside a lake or reservoir of at least 100 ha.

Reaches confirmed by hand are then added. Last, rearing is kept only where it connects to
spawning: spawning anywhere upstream, or within 10 km downstream with no stretch of 5 % or steeper
between them.
Channel width is modelled only on streams of order 2 and up, so the stream test never admits a
small, unmeasured first-order stream.

Only the stream test is tuned here. Wetlands and lakes keep their tests. River polygons keep
theirs too, except that they share the stream test's gradient maximum, so a new maximum moves
them as well, though the tuning scored no visit in a river polygon.

## What evidence is used?

The province's stream atlas divides British Columbia into **watershed groups**, large basins such
as the Bulkley. They are the unit everything below is counted in and tested on.

The evidence is the provincial Fisheries Data Information System (FDIS) electrofishing records,
placed on `link`'s stream segments. A visit counts when it is on the kind of stream the stream
test covers, outside wetlands of 1 ha or more and lakes of 100 ha or more. It must have a fished
area of 10 to 10,000 m², and be in a group where `link` expects chinook. It must also have no
natural barrier to chinook downstream, and no record code that could hide a catch. After checks
on placement, date and effort, that leaves `r n0(summ$visits_in)` visits in `r summ$groups`
groups. A group where chinook were always or never caught cannot tell rules apart, so the tests
use the `r summ$groups_both` groups with both outcomes: **`r n0(dflt$n_visits)` visits, of which
`r n0(dflt$n_detect)` caught chinook**.

## Which rules were tried?

Each candidate rule sets three things, the same three `default` sets:

- **a size floor**: a mean annual flow (MAD, modelled) of
  `r lst(sort(unique(tune$size_min[tune$size_var == "mad"])), "or")` m³/s, or a channel width of
  `r lst(sort(unique(tune$size_min[tune$size_var == "width"])), "or")` m;
- **a gradient maximum** of `r lst(grad(sort(unique(tune$grad_max))), "or")`;
- **a near-a-river exception**: none, or a stream below the size floor still counts when a river of
  at least Q m³/s is within D m downstream (Q of `r lst(sort(unique(na.omit(tune$exc_q))), "or")`;
  D of `r lst(format(sort(unique(na.omit(tune$exc_d))), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), "or")`).

Every combination is one rule, `r n0(nrow(tune))` in all, `default` among them. The exception is
there because juvenile chinook move up from large rivers into small streams close by.

## How is a rule scored?

A rule is worth having if it predicts where chinook are caught in a watershed it was not built
from. So the `r summ$groups_both` groups are split at random into `r meta$spec$folds` sets,
called **folds**. A model learns how much the rule matters from four folds and predicts the
visits in the fifth, and this repeats until every group has been predicted once. The model also
allows for fished area, data set and era. Each held-out group's own overall catch rate is the one
thing fitted on its own visits, and that costs every rule the same.

The **score** adds up, over every predicted visit, how far the prediction was from what the crew
found (the deviance). Lower is better. Only differences between rules matter: the model with no
rule at all scores `r n1(-rec$ddev_null)` worse than the best rule.

## Which rules can the data not tell apart?

Scores carry noise: another set of watersheds would rank close rules differently. So the choice is
not simply the best score. Every rule within one standard error of the best, measured across
watershed groups, is kept. That set is the **region**: the rules the records cannot rank. It
holds `r nrow(region)` rules, all of one shape:

- a flow floor of `r min(region$size_min)` to `r max(region$size_min)` m³/s, never a width floor;
- the exception, with a river of `r min(region$exc_q)` to `r max(region$exc_q)` m³/s within
  `r km_d(min(region$exc_d))` to `r km_d(max(region$exc_d))`;
- a gradient maximum of `r lst(grad(sort(unique(region$grad_max))), "or")`.

`default` scores `r n1(dflt$ddev_best)` worse than the best rule, with a standard error of
`r n1(dflt$se_diff)`, so it is outside the region.

```{r profile, fig.height = 5.2, fig.cap = "How good each value of each setting can be. Each point is the best score of any rule using that value, as deviance above the best rule, so lower is better. A filled point has at least one rule in the region. A ring marks the value default uses."}
comp <- function(lab, v, key) {
  tune |>
    mutate(value = v) |>
    group_by(value, key = key) |>
    summarise(best = min(ddev_best), in_region = any(in_region), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(part = lab)
}
size_lab <- paste(ifelse(tune$size_var == "mad", "MAD", "width"), as.character(tune$size_min))
size_key <- ifelse(tune$size_var == "mad", tune$size_min, 10 + tune$size_min)
prof <- bind_rows(
  comp("Size floor (m³/s or m)", size_lab, size_key),
  comp("Gradient maximum", grad(tune$grad_max), tune$grad_max),
  comp("Exception: river size Q (m³/s)", ifelse(is.na(tune$exc_q), "none", format(tune$exc_q, trim = TRUE)),
       ifelse(is.na(tune$exc_q), -1, tune$exc_q)),
  comp("Exception: distance D (m)", ifelse(is.na(tune$exc_d), "none", format(tune$exc_d, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)),
       ifelse(is.na(tune$exc_d), -1, tune$exc_d))
)
prof$part <- factor(prof$part, levels = unique(prof$part))
prof <- prof |> group_by(part) |> mutate(value = factor(value, levels = unique(value[order(key)]))) |> ungroup()
dflt_vals <- tibble(
  part = factor(levels(prof$part), levels = levels(prof$part)),
  value = c(paste("width", as.character(dflt$size_min)), grad(dflt$grad_max), "none", "none")
)
dpts <- inner_join(prof, dflt_vals, by = c("part", "value"))
ggplot(prof, aes(value, best)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(fill = in_region), shape = 21, size = 2.6, colour = "grey20") +
  geom_point(data = dpts, shape = 21, size = 5, stroke = 1, colour = "#d95f02", fill = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#1b6ca8", `FALSE` = "white"),
                    labels = c(`TRUE` = "a rule in the region", `FALSE` = "none in the region"), name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~part, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Deviance above the best rule") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## Which rule is recommended?

The choice was fixed before any rule was scored: from the region, the rule closest to `default`.
Every rule in the region differs from `default` in all three settings, so the best scorer is
recommended. The new rule calls fewer visits habitat and takes in as many catches:

```{r raw}
raw <- bind_rows(dflt, rec) |>
  transmute(Rule = c("default", "recommended"),
            `Visits it calls habitat` = n0(n_in), `Of those, chinook caught` = n0(n_detect_in),
            `Catch rate on habitat` = pc(raw_rate_in, 1), `Catch rate elsewhere` = pc(raw_rate_out, 1))
knitr::kable(raw, align = "lrrrr",
             caption = paste0("What each rule calls habitat among the ", n0(dflt$n_visits), " visits tested."))
```

## How firm is the choice?

Three checks, fixed before the run, ask whether the choice rests on chance or on reusing the same
data to choose and to score.

- **Other random splits.** The split into folds is random, set by a number called a seed.
  Scored again on `r nrow(seeds)` other seeds, the recommended rule is in the region on
  `r sum(seeds$main_rec_in_region)` of them and `default` on `r sum(seeds$default_in_region)`.
  `r seed_same_shape` of the `r nrow(seeds)` pick the same rule at a different gradient; the other
  picks `r words(seed_other[1, ])`.
- **Choosing on some groups, scoring on others.** Choosing a rule on four folds and scoring it on
  the fifth, the chosen rule beats `default` in `r sum(honest$dev_rec < honest$dev_default)` of the
  `r nrow(honest)` folds, and `r if (sum(honest$dev_rec) < sum(honest$dev_default)) "beats it" else "loses to it"`
  over all five together. The separation is partial, because each fold's choice
  leans on scores from models that had seen that fold.
- **Drawing the groups again.** Repeating the choice on `r meta$spec$n_boot` random redraws of
  the groups, the exact recommended rule comes back `r pc(rec$boot_rec_share)` of the time, but
  its parts are steadier: a flow floor in `r pc(sum(tune$boot_rec_share[tune$size_var == "mad"]))`
  of draws, `r rec$size_min` m³/s in `r pc(share_of("size_min", rec$size_min))`, and a
  `r rec$exc_q` m³/s river in `r pc(share_of("exc_q", rec$exc_q))`. The gradient maximum varies
  most: `r grad(rec$grad_max)` in `r pc(share_of("grad_max", rec$grad_max))`, `r grad(0.07)` in
  `r pc(share_of("grad_max", 0.07))`, and `default`'s `r grad(dflt$grad_max)` in
  `r pc(share_of("grad_max", dflt$grad_max))`.

The shape is settled: a flow floor near `r rec$size_min` m³/s and an exception for small streams
near a river. The gradient maximum is the least settled part.

## Why does a nearby river matter?

After the choice, one model was fitted to the visits that carry a modelled flow, with flow and
distance to a river of at least `r meta$curve_ref$q` m³/s as one surface. The table reads the
fitted chance of a catch on one standard visit. It stops below `r meta$curve_ref$q` m³/s, because a
stream that size is itself the river:

```{r surface-tab}
sf_ <- x$surface
dists <- sort(unique(sf_$dist_m))
st <- tibble(`Stream flow (m³/s)` = format(sort(unique(sf_$size)), trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE))
for (dm in dists) {
  col <- if (dm >= meta$curve_ref$dist_cap_m) paste(km_d(dm), "or more") else km_d(dm)
  st[[col]] <- pc(sf_$rate[sf_$dist_m == dm][order(sf_$size[sf_$dist_m == dm])], 1)
}
knitr::kable(st, align = paste0("l", strrep("r", length(dists))),
             caption = paste0("The fitted chance of catching chinook on one standard visit, by stream flow (rows) and by ",
                              "distance downstream to a river of at least ", meta$curve_ref$q, " m³/s (columns), at a ",
                              "gradient of ", grad(meta$curve_ref$gradient), "."))
r_at <- function(s, dm) sf_$rate[sf_$size == s & sf_$dist_m == dm]
near <- sf_$rate[sf_$dist_m == min(dists)]
```

Within `r km_d(min(dists))` of a river the chance is about the same whatever the stream's flow,
`r pc(min(near), 1)` to `r pc(max(near), 1)`. Ten kilometres away it rises with flow, from
`r pc(r_at(min(sf_$size), 10000), 1)` at `r min(sf_$size)` m³/s to `r pc(r_at(max(sf_$size), 10000), 1)` at
`r max(sf_$size)` m³/s. That is the
shape the recommended rule draws: beside a river a small stream counts, and away from one only a
stream above the floor does. The chance falls off past a few hundred metres from the river, so
`r km_d(rec$exc_d)` sits on the way down. Steepness matters less: at `r grad(0.09)` the chance is
about `r pc(grad_at(0.09) / grad_at(0.02))` of what it is at `r grad(0.02)`. The model fits smooth
curves, so it cannot show a step at a threshold; each threshold is where habitat and non-habitat
separate best on held-out groups, a cut across a slope. For the gradient that is at the edge of
what was tried: `r grad(max(tune$grad_max))` is the steepest maximum scored, and nothing steeper
was.

## What does it change on the ground?

Both rules were run through all of `link`'s steps on every one of the `r nrow(per_group)`
watershed groups `link` classifies for chinook.

```{r km}
ch <- x$change |>
  group_by(direction, reason) |>
  summarise(km_all = sum(km), km_1 = sum(km[order == "1"]), .groups = "drop")
lost_size <- ch$km_all[ch$direction == "lost" & grepl("^size", ch$reason)]
gain_exc <- ch$km_all[ch$direction == "gained" & grepl("^exception", ch$reason)]
gain_exc_1 <- ch$km_1[ch$direction == "gained" & grepl("^exception", ch$reason)]
km_t <- tibble(
  ` ` = c("Habitat under default", "Habitat under the recommended rule",
          "Lost, all reasons", "Lost: wide enough for default, below the flow floor, no river close",
          "Gained, all reasons", "Gained through the exception (small streams near a river)",
          "Gained through the exception, on first-order streams"),
  km = n0(c(all_row$default_km, all_row$tuned_km, all_row$lost_km, lost_size, all_row$gained_km, gain_exc, gain_exc_1)))
knitr::kable(km_t, align = "lr",
             caption = paste("Chinook rearing habitat in km under each rule, over all", nrow(per_group), "watershed groups."))
```

The change varies by group, from `r n1(min(per_group$change_pct))` % to
`r n1(max(per_group$change_pct))` %; `r sum(per_group$change_pct > 0)` of the
`r nrow(per_group)` groups gain. In the Bulkley the recommended rule draws
`r n0(map_row$tuned_km)` km against `default`'s `r n0(map_row$default_km)`
(`r n1(map_row$change_pct)` %).

```{r zoom}
# the window: the 12 km square, on a grid offset by half a window, holding the most km of whichever
# of lost and gained is smaller, so the detail shows both
w <- 12000
cen <- sf::st_coordinates(suppressWarnings(sf::st_point_on_surface(seg)))
lost_l <- seg$length_metre * (seg$flag_default & !seg$flag_tuned)
gain_l <- seg$length_metre * (!seg$flag_default & seg$flag_tuned)
cand <- do.call(rbind, lapply(list(c(0, 0), c(0.5, 0), c(0, 0.5), c(0.5, 0.5)), function(o) {
  kx <- floor(cen[, 1] / w - o[1])
  ky <- floor(cen[, 2] / w - o[2])
  k <- paste(kx, ky)
  sc <- pmin(tapply(lost_l, k, sum), tapply(gain_l, k, sum))
  i <- which.max(sc)
  kk <- as.numeric(strsplit(names(sc)[i], " ")[[1]])
  data.frame(x0 = (kk[1] + o[1]) * w, y0 = (kk[2] + o[2]) * w, score = sc[i])
}))
best <- cand[which.max(cand$score), ]
box <- sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = best$x0, ymin = best$y0, xmax = best$x0 + w,
                                                        ymax = best$y0 + w), crs = 3005)))
seg_z <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_crop(seg, box))
water_z <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_crop(water, box))

# one example per case inside the window: the segment meeting the case's conditions with the most length
# inside the window, on the stream test's own edges, and with neither rule's verdict changed by the hand-entered
# reaches or the connectivity pass, so its row in the table explains both verdicts
in_w <- seg[seg$id_segment %in% seg_z$id_segment, ]
in_w$len_in <- as.numeric(sf::st_length(seg_z[match(in_w$id_segment, seg_z$id_segment), ]))
in_w <- in_w[in_w$edge_type %in% c(1000, 1100, 2000, 2300) & (in_w$pre_default == in_w$flag_default) %in% TRUE & (in_w$pre_tuned == in_w$flag_tuned) %in% TRUE, ]
cases <- list(
  "Kept by both" = with(in_w, flag_default & flag_tuned & mad >= rec$size_min & channel_width >= dflt$size_min &
                          gradient <= dflt$grad_max),
  "Lost: below the flow floor, no river close" = with(in_w, flag_default & !flag_tuned & mad < rec$size_min &
                                                          (is.na(dist_m) | dist_m > rec$exc_d)),
  "Gained: small stream near a river" = with(in_w, !flag_default & flag_tuned & mad < rec$size_min &
                                                 !is.na(dist_m) & dist_m <= rec$exc_d))
ex <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(cases), function(k) {
  i <- which(cases[[k]] %in% TRUE)
  if (!length(i)) return(NULL)
  r <- in_w[i[which.max(in_w$len_in[i])], ]
  r$case <- k
  r
}))
ex$label <- as.character(seq_len(nrow(ex)))
# marker on the part of each segment inside the window, so a segment crossing its edge is still marked
ex_in <- seg_z[match(ex$id_segment, seg_z$id_segment), ]
ex_pts <- sf::st_sf(label = ex$label, geometry = suppressWarnings(sf::st_point_on_surface(sf::st_geometry(ex_in))))
```

```{r map, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.6, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = paste0("Chinook rearing in the Bulkley (", meta$map_group, ") under each rule: kept by both, lost (default only) and gained (the legend's 'tuned only', meaning the recommended rule only). Left, the whole group with the window outlined; right, the ", w / 1000, " km window, with the numbered examples the table below describes. Line width follows stream order.")}
f1 <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
f2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
knw_compare_map(seg, water, png = f1, panels = "rules", mark = box)
knw_compare_map(seg_z, water_z, png = f2, panels = "rules", lwd = 2.5, legend = FALSE, labels = ex_pts)
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout = grid::grid.layout(1, 2)))
grid::grid.raster(png::readPNG(f1), vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 1))
grid::grid.raster(png::readPNG(f2), vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 2))
```

```{r examples}
f_num <- function(v, d) ifelse(is.na(v), NA, formatC(v, format = "fg", digits = d))
yes_no <- function(v) ifelse(v, "habitat", "not habitat")
ex_t <- tibble(
  `#` = ex$label,
  Case = ex$case,
  `Flow (m³/s)` = f_num(ex$mad, 2),
  `Channel width (m)` = ifelse(is.na(ex$channel_width), "none modelled", f_num(ex$channel_width, 2)),
  Gradient = grad(round(ex$gradient, 4)),
  `Downstream to a river` = vapply(seq_len(nrow(ex)), function(i) {
    d <- ex$dist_m[i]
    if (!is.na(d)) km_d(signif(d, 2)) else if (ex$mad[i] >= rec$size_min) "not needed" else "no river found"
  }, ""),
  default = yes_no(ex$flag_default),
  Recommended = yes_no(ex$flag_tuned))
knitr::kable(ex_t, align = "llrrrrll",
             caption = paste0("The numbered segments on the map: what each rule reads and what each decides. ",
                              "default needs a channel at least ", dflt$size_min, " m wide and a gradient of at most ",
                              grad(dflt$grad_max), "; the recommended rule needs a gradient of at most ",
                              grad(rec$grad_max), " and a flow of at least ", rec$size_min, " m³/s, or a river of at least ",
                              rec$exc_q, " m³/s within ", km_d(rec$exc_d), " downstream. The distance is to the first ",
                              "such river downstream, measured only where the exception could apply."))
gain_grad <- ch$km_all[ch$direction == "gained" & grepl("^gradient", ch$reason)]
gain_flow <- ch$km_all[ch$direction == "gained" & grepl("^size: tuned passes", ch$reason)]
```

The examples show what both rules keep and the two largest changes. Two smaller kinds of gain are not
among them:
streams between `r grad(dflt$grad_max)` and `r grad(rec$grad_max)` steep, which only the new gradient
maximum admits (`r n0(gain_grad)` km across the province), and streams whose flow passes the floor
where `default`'s width test fails or has no width (`r n0(gain_flow)` km).

Orange is mostly the upper reaches of tributaries: flow grows downstream, so a tributary keeps its
lower reach and loses the part where its flow falls below the floor more than `r km_d(rec$exc_d)`
from a river. Green is short reaches of small streams beside a river, which the exception adds.

```{r checks}
ck <- x$checks
fv <- ck[ck$check == "fdis_visits", ]
rate <- function(r, s) {
  v <- fv[fv$rule == r & fv$segment == s, ]
  v$n_detect / v$n
}
ob <- ck[ck$check == "bcfishobs_outside", ]
```

**Two checks.** On the `r n0(sum(fv$n[fv$rule == "default"]))` electrofishing visits with a fished
area of 10 to 10,000 m² on accessible streams (wetland lines included), canals, reservoir banks
and river lines in the `r nrow(per_group)` groups, chinook were caught on
`r pc(rate("tuned", "rearing"))` of visits on the recommended rule's habitat and
`r pc(rate("tuned", "accessible_not_rearing"), 1)` elsewhere, against
`r pc(rate("default", "rearing"))` and `r pc(rate("default", "accessible_not_rearing"), 1)` for
`default`. These visits overlap the ones the tuning scored, so this shows the rule does what it
was chosen to do.
Other sources record chinook at `r n0(ob$n[1])` places within 100 m of an accessible single-line
stream or canal not drawn through a wetland, spawning-only places left out; no rule was scored on them. The share of those places on the
recommended rule's habitat is `r n1(ob$lift[ob$rule == "tuned"])` times the rule's share of that
stream length, against `r n1(ob$lift[ob$rule == "default"])` for `default`.

## What the recommendation is not

- **Not applied yet.** `link` changes nothing until a configuration reads the new thresholds
  ([link#346](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/link/issues/346)).
- **Juveniles caught by electrofishing, on streams.** Spawning is outside it. Wetlands and lakes
  keep their own tests; river polygons take the new gradient maximum, which the tuning scored on
  streams only.
- **Better separation, less extent.** The score rewards a rule whose habitat and non-habitat
  differ most, not one that leaves nothing out: `r pc(rec$raw_rate_out, 1)` of visits outside the
  new rule still caught chinook.
- **A cut on a slope.** Values next to the recommended ones are nearly as good; the region gives
  the range.
- **One run of `link`**, `r meta$link_run_uid`. Distances were scored from each visit; on `link`'s
  segments they are measured from each segment's downstream end, which is a little looser.
- **Habitat, not use.** A 0 to 1 grade of expected use per segment was also published, but it
  currently understates large streams near rivers and is being redone.

## Software and how to cite it

- [`link`](`r link_site`): the habitat model and its configurations.
- [`fresh`](`r fresh_site`): runs `link`'s rules on the BC Freshwater Atlas.
- `knowledge`: the fish records, the tests and this article. It has no DOI yet; cite it as:

```{r cite, results = "asis"}
cat(format(utils::citation("knowledge"), style = "text"), sep = "\n\n")
```
